Theorem
[Finite propagation speed] 1. ch2:2.4-thm-6\group Energy Methods If $u\in C^2$ solves the homogeneous wave equation and $u=u_t=0$ on $B(x_0,t_0) imes \{ 0\} $, then $u=0$ throughout $C$.
Proof

\sketch Define the local energy

\[ e(t)= rac12\int _{B(x_0,t_0-t)}(u_t^2+|Du|^2)\, dx. \]

Differentiation over the shrinking ball, integration by parts, and the wave equation give

\[ e'(t)=\int _{\partial B(x_0,t_0-t)} \left( rac{\partial u}{\partial u }u_t- rac12u_t^2- rac12|Du|^2 ight)dS. \]

Since $|\partial _ u u\, u_t|\le (u_t^2+|Du|^2)/2$, one has $e'\le 0$. The initial assumptions give $e(0)=0$, hence $u_t=Du=0$ and then $u=0$ in the cone.

□
